name: Coming of Age Day
venue: Citywide · photo crowds at Meiji Jingu
desc: National holiday: 20-year-olds in furisode and suits fill shrines and photo spots. Ceremonies are invitation-only; streets and Meiji Jingu are free to watch. Best mid-morning for photos. Crowds, not a kids’ festival. Price: free to watch.

name: Dezome-shiki firefighters
desc: Tokyo Fire Department New Year parade at Tokyo Big Sight. Ladder acrobatics, trucks, band and water displays. About 2 hours outdoors. Best viewed from the public plaza; arrive early for a front spot. Price: free.

name: Daikon Radish Festival
desc: Temple memorial with cooked furofuki daikon and amazake after the service. Short, local, and warm on a cold January day. Shoes off inside the hall. Go around midday when food is served; portions can run out. Price: free (small donation welcome).

name: Grand Sumo Hatsu Basho
desc: January tournament at Ryogoku Kokugikan, 10–24 Jan. In this week: Sun 10 and Mon 11 only. Full-day session from morning to late afternoon. English programme sold on site. Book weeks ahead. Price: usually ¥3,800–¥14,800; many days sell out.

name: Tondoyaki bonfire
desc: Neighbourhood burning of New Year pine decorations. Drums, “Tondo!” shouts, roast mochi over the fire. Stand well back from sparks. Late afternoon into evening; dress for smoke and cold. Price: free.

name: Hashigo-nori ladders
desc: Traditional firefighter ladder stunts during a local shrine or temple rite. Shorter and closer than Dezome-shiki. A few set pieces, then the ceremony continues. Good if you already plan that neighbourhood that morning. Price: free.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Yanaka)
desc: Walk seven small Yanaka shrines and temples and collect goshuin stamps. Quiet old-town streets, cats, and snack shops between stops. 2–3 hours on foot. Each stamp book page is paid separately at the desk. Price: shrines free; goshuin about ¥300–¥500 each.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Nihonbashi)
desc: One of the shortest lucky-gods loops, in the old merchant district. Most stops are close to Tokyo Station and department-store food halls. Doable in about 2 hours if you do not queue for every seal. Price: shrines free; goshuin about ¥300–¥500 each.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Asakusa)
desc: Compact pilgrimage around Senso-ji and nearby halls. Easy scavenger-hunt style walk with a 10-year-old. Combine with Nakamise snacks. Senso-ji grounds are busy even in January. Price: grounds free; goshuin about ¥300–¥500 each.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Kameido)
desc: Eastern Tokyo circuit that usually starts at Kameido Tenjin. Plum buds may just be showing. Fewer tourists than Asakusa. Allow a half day including the train from central Tokyo. Price: shrines free; goshuin about ¥300–¥500 each.

name: Ueno antique market
desc: Aozora Kotto-ichi in Ueno Park: ceramics, kimono, old books, vintage clothes. Outdoor stalls, cash useful, some English. Pair with the zoo or science museum. Morning is less picked-over. Price: free to enter; bargaining on goods.

name: GUNDAM-Con 2027
desc: Gundam 50th-anniversary convention: exhibits, stages, Gunpla and game events. Ticketed indoor day. Check the official sale for age limits on some stages. Better for a fan than a first-time tourist. Price: paid convention ticket; confirm on the official site.

name: Cinnamoroll Park
desc: Sanrio indoor park: giant Cinnamoroll slide, photo spots, games. Timed entry. 1–2 hours is enough. Shop and café extra. Good rainy-day pick for a 10-year-old who likes characters. Price: timed ticket, typically a few thousand yen; book ahead.

name: Tokyo Mega Illumination
desc: Large winter light park plus evening miniature-horse photos (about 17:30–19:00). Allow 1.5–2 hours after dark. Weeknights are less packed. Pair with a nearby dinner; it is not a city-centre walk. Price: paid admission; check the official calendar for the 2026–27 rate.

name: Tokyo Disney Resort
desc: Disneyland and DisneySea. Full-day outing; book dated tickets in advance. Parade and night-show times change; check the app that morning. January weekdays are calmer than weekends. Price: dated tickets, typically about ¥7,900–¥10,900 by calendar.

name: Ghibli Museum
desc: Cat Bus (small children only), short film, rooftop robot. No indoor photos. Timed Lawson tickets go on sale at 10:00 on the 10th for the next month. Closed Tuesdays as a rule. About 1.5–2 hours inside. Price: 19+ ¥1,000; 13–18 ¥700; 7–12 ¥400; 4–6 ¥100; under 4 free.

name: Midtown Ice Rink
desc: Largest outdoor real-ice rink in central Tokyo, Roppongi Midtown. Gloves required. Rental skates extra. Evening lights are the nicest. Sessions last about 90 minutes; buy the next session if you want longer. Price: entry plus rental, typically about ¥2,000–¥3,000.

name: Meiji Jingu Gaien rink
desc: Full-size indoor rink. Weather-proof and easy from Aoyama / Gaienmae. Weekday sessions are quieter. Helmets sometimes available to rent. Allow time to put on skates and store bags. Price: ticket plus rental about ¥2,200 on weekdays; more on holidays.

name: Tatsumi Ice Arena
desc: Tokyo’s largest indoor arena, two rinks, public sessions most days. Closed 1 Jan and often the third Monday. Farther out, more ice time. Good if the child already skates. Price: public session about ¥1,300–¥1,600; rental extra.

name: Winter Wonder Park
desc: Harbor-side rink (resin surface in recent winters). Ages 3+. Short session, views of the waterfront. Combine with Odaiba / teamLab Planets. Wind can be cold on the deck. Price: last season about ¥1,200 including rental; confirm this winter.

name: Shin-Yokohama Skate Center
desc: International-size indoor rink and cheap public sessions. Easy if you already visit the ramen museum next door. Morning weekday ice is the emptiest. Price: public skate often under ¥1,500 plus rental.

name: Marunouchi Illumination
desc: Champagne-gold trees from Tokyo Station toward the Imperial Palace. Free evening street walk. 30–60 minutes. Pair with a station meal. Best after 17:30 in early January. Price: free.

name: Hibiya Magic Time
desc: Entertainment-district winter lights around Hibiya and Yurakucho. Flat, short loop. Easy after an Imperial Palace walk or a concert. Photo spots get busy at dusk. Price: free.

name: Ebisu Garden Place lights
desc: Covered courtyard illuminations at Ebisu Garden Place. Indoor-adjacent, good if it rains. Combine with Ebisu / Daikanyama dinner. Shorter than Marunouchi; 20–40 minutes. Price: free to walk the courtyard.

name: Relaxing Aquarium Dream Day
desc: Special aquarium day with a calmer programme (check that week’s hours). Better for watching than touching. Indoor and warm. Confirm the exact date on the official page before you go. Price: standard aquarium ticket unless a separate event fee is listed.

name: Ueno Zoo
desc: Children’s zoo, elephants, polar bears, shoebill. No giant pandas right now. Cheap metropolitan tickets. Pair with the antique market or science museum. 2–3 hours is plenty. Go at opening if you want the small-animal area first. Price: adults ¥600; junior high ¥200; elementary and under often free.

name: Tama Zoological Park
desc: Wide, walkable zoo: lions, koalas, insectarium. Full-day trip west of Tokyo. Less crowded than Ueno. Bring snacks; it is a lot of walking in the cold. Pair with a Keio line day. Price: adults ¥600; junior high ¥200; elementary and under often free.

name: Inokashira Park Zoo
desc: Small zoo split across the park, next to the Ghibli Museum. Guinea pigs, birds, a tiny amusement bit. 45–90 minutes. Combine with Kichijoji eating streets. Price: adults ¥400; children lower; park itself is free.

name: Sumida Aquarium
desc: Indoor tanks under Tokyo Skytree. Penguins, sea lions, jellyfish. 1.5–2 hours. Easy if you already climb the Skytree. Weekday mornings are quietest. Price: adults about ¥2,400; children less; combo tickets with Skytree exist.

name: Sunshine Aquarium
desc: Rooftop aquarium on Sunshine City, Ikebukuro. Seals and a sky deck. 1.5 hours. Indoor mall food downstairs. Good if weather is poor and you are already in Ikebukuro. Price: adults about ¥2,500; children less.
